secondary_sources: Reference_web/3.15.3/index.html (bootstrap theme script, meta theme-color #161616/#f8f8f8, inline <style>)
_meta.stack: React + Tailwind CSS v4 + lucide icons (minified production bundle)

conversion.oklch_to_srgb: oklch -> oklab (polar to cartesian) -> linear sRGB via the exact Oklab matrices from Bjorn Ottosson's reference (https://bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab/) -> gamma-encoded sRGB using the IEC 61966-2-1 / CSS Color 4 transfer function (x<=0.0031308 ? 12.92x : 1.055*x^(1/2.4)-0.055) -> per-channel clamp to [0,1] -> 8-bit round-half-up.
conversion.oklab_to_srgb: linear sRGB via the exact Oklab inverse matrices, then the same gamma + clamp + round steps.
conversion.color_mix: CSS Color Module Level 4 color-mix(): premultiplied-alpha interpolation in the declared space (oklab for most tokens, srgb for the usage-heatmap tokens), weights normalised to sum 100%.
conversion.clamping: per-channel clamp (naive gamut clipping), NOT the CSS Color 4 chroma-reduction gamut mapping algorithm.
conversion.precision: float64 throughout; 8-bit output rounded half-up. Worst observed deviation vs Chromium: 1 LSB.
conversion.rounding_note: round-half-up is deliberate: Python's built-in round() is half-to-even and turns alpha 0.7 into 178 instead of the browser's 179.

validation.method: Every resolved colour was compared against a real Chromium CSS engine (Microsoft Edge --headless=new) fed the unmodified snapshot stylesheet and asked for the computed colour of each custom property under each theme class.
validation.scope: All 311 --color-* tokens x 2 themes = 622 potential comparisons; 616 were comparable and all 616 agreed. The remaining 6 are 3 numeric --color-*-opacity tokens that have no colour to compare. The 240 non --color-* variables (gradients, shadows, --tw-prose-*, Tailwind internals, typography/spacing) were NOT compared one by one; most are not single colours.

palette_conversion_spot_check.note: Direct OKLCH->sRGB comparison for the 125 palette tokens whose value is a raw oklch() literal. The CSS Color 4 gamut-mapping algorithm scores worse (116/125), so naive per-channel clamping was chosen.

validation.note: Tailwind's own emitted sRGB fallback hexes in the bundle are stale (they match an older Tailwind converter: red-600 fallback #E40014 while the CSS engine renders #E7000B). The values here follow the engine, which is what the UI actually paints.

caveats: --tw-prose-* dark values are a modelling inference: their dark branch lives under @media (prefers-color-scheme:dark), so they follow the OS preference rather than the .dark class. They are attributed to `dark` here on the assumption that the OS preference matches the app theme; if the two diverge in a real browser they split.

This build compiles every `dark:` utility variant to @media (prefers-color-scheme:dark); there are zero class-based `:where(.dark ...)` variants. Semantic tokens therefore switch on the .dark class while `dark:` utilities switch on the OS preference.

cascade_model.description: Effective light/dark values are computed with an explicit cascade: unlayered rules beat @layer rules; within the same layer/specificity the later byte offset wins; @supports (color:color-mix(...)) branches always apply in modern engines and sit after their fallback, so they win.
